title: Modals (meanings + perfect)
note: Mega unit: obligation / no obligation / prohibition (must, have to, mustn't, needn't, had to, will have to) · permission + ability (can, could, be allowed to, be able to, let, make, managed to) · advice (should, ought to, had better) · deduction now (must, can't, might, may, could) · modal perfect (modal + have + past participle) · 5 strands x 12 · 60 items · built to live 2026-08-06 (cloud run 6)

items.en: I must finish this report today.
items.gap: I ____ finish this report today.
accepts: I must finish this report today.
items.explanation: must and have to both express obligation; have to is the one with a full set of forms.
items.explanation_cz: must i have to vyjadřují povinnost; have to je to sloveso, které má všechny tvary.

items.en: She has to work on Saturday.
items.gap: She ____ to work on Saturday.
accepts: She has to work on Saturday.
He has to work on Saturday.
They have to work on Saturday.
items.explanation: must and have to both express obligation; have to is the one with a full set of forms.
items.explanation_cz: must i have to vyjadřují povinnost; have to je to sloveso, které má všechny tvary.

items.en: We had to wait two hours.
items.gap: We ____ to wait two hours.
accepts: We had to wait two hours.
items.explanation: must has no past form — the past of both must and have to is had to.
items.explanation_cz: must nemá minulý tvar — minulostí pro must i have to je had to.

items.en: You mustn't park in front of the gate.
items.gap: You ____ park in front of the gate.
accepts: You mustn't park in front of the gate.
You must not park in front of the gate.
items.explanation: mustn't = it is forbidden. Do not confuse it with don't have to.
items.explanation_cz: mustn't = je to zakázané. Nepleťte si to s don't have to.

items.en: You don't have to come if you are busy.

You do not have to come if you're busy.
items.explanation: don't have to = there is no obligation; you may do it or not.
items.explanation_cz: don't have to = žádná povinnost; můžete, ale nemusíte.

items.en: You needn't worry about the cost.

cards.title: One small set of verbs, six different jobs
cards.title_cz: Malá skupina sloves, šest různých úloh
cards.body: Modal verbs (**must, can, could, may, might, should, will, would**) add an attitude to the main verb: how necessary, how allowed, how likely. They take the **base form** after them and never add -s. Where a modal has no tense you need, a **semi-modal** — have to, be able to, be allowed to — steps in.
cards.body_cz: Modální slovesa (**must, can, could, may, might, should, will, would**) přidávají k významovému slovesu postoj: jak je to nutné, jak dovolené, jak pravděpodobné. Po nich jde **základní tvar** a nikdy neberou -s. Když modální sloveso nemá potřebný čas, nastoupí **polomodální** vazba — have to, be able to, be allowed to.

table.caption: The six jobs
rows: can, could, be allowed to, be able to
He must be stuck in traffic.

cards.title: The two negatives that are not opposites
cards.body: This is the single most expensive modal mistake. **mustn't** forbids the action. **don't have to** removes the obligation and leaves you free. Czech *nemusíš* matches the second one, which is exactly why the first gets picked by accident.
cards.body_cz: Tohle je nejdražší chyba u modálních sloves. **mustn't** činnost zakazuje. **don't have to** ruší povinnost a nechává vám volnost. České *nemusíš* odpovídá tomu druhému — a právě proto se omylem sahá po tom prvním.
points: You mustn't tell her. (it is forbidden — keep it secret)
You don't have to tell her. (up to you — no obligation)
needn't = don't have to, and takes the base form with no to
must has no past and no future: had to, will have to

cards.title: let and make take the base form
cards.title_cz: let a make berou základní tvar
cards.body: **let** and **make** are followed by a person and then the **base form with no to** — the same shape as a modal. Their polite relatives, **allow** and **force**, do take *to*. Mixing the two shapes is the usual slip.
cards.body_cz: Po **let** a **make** jde osoba a pak **základní tvar bez to** — stejný tvar jako po modálním slovese. Jejich zdvořilejší protějšky **allow** a **force** naopak *to* vyžadují. Právě záměna těchto dvou vzorců je běžná chyba.
points: My parents let me stay out late. (not: let me to stay)
The teacher made us rewrite it. (not: made us to rewrite)
They allowed me to stay. · They forced us to rewrite it.
In the passive, make regains the to: we were made to rewrite it

cards.title: Deduction: how sure are you?
cards.body: For a conclusion drawn from evidence, the modal reports your confidence. Note the negative: the opposite of **must be** is **can't be**, never *mustn't be*. Move the whole scale into the past by adding **have + past participle**.
cards.body_cz: U závěru z důkazů modální sloveso vyjadřuje míru jistoty. Pozor na zápor: opakem **must be** je **can't be**, nikdy *mustn't be*. Celou škálu posunete do minulosti přidáním **have + příčestí minulé**.

table.caption: Avoid / Say
rows: You don't have to smoke here.
He mustn't be at home — his phone is off.
He **can't** be at home — his phone is off.
They let me to borrow it.
I could fix the printer in the end.
I **managed to** fix the printer in the end.
one successful past action, not general ability
